packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-08 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or
reading of this text. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files in this packet
(plus a directory listing of the packet folder and a pixel-size check). I did
not use the web, any catalogue, or packet.json. I have not named a work or
author; where the prose quotes or paraphrases scripture-like phrases I have
transcribed them as seen and not supplied missing words.

Conventions: (abc) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain reading;
[illegible] = could not read; [?] = a letter group seen but not resolved.
Line numbers count text lines from the top of each tile. Tiles overlap;
repeated lines are marked "= image-NNN Lx".

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
======================================================================
One leaf fragment, two faces (overviews image-001 and image-006), landscape
as photographed: the fragment is wider than tall and has been cut down, so
each face shows only part of two columns (about 15-16 lines per column).
Protogothic/early Gothic book hand, brown-black ink, no colour visible.
Columns are of equal width; ruling and prickings visible at the outer edges
(image-001 left and right, image-006 right). Upper and lower edges folded
over (binding turn-ins); on face 1 the lowest 2-3 lines of each column lie on
the folded strip.
Face 1 (image-001): pencil "Stams, STA, Fog. 74r" top right; pencil at lower
left "VI d/L, 19" and a word + "1620"? (modern notes, partly hidden by the
colour chart). A paper/parchment patch is glued over the upper middle of col.
a (image-002), hiding text; a second loss/patch lower in col. a (image-003).
Faint brown marginal notes right of col. b: "S cp v"? beside image-004 L7,
"A mb[...] / ad rom[...]"? beside image-005 L8-L9, and "I. [...]" beside
image-005 L13 (small later hand; read only partly).
Face 2 (image-006): pencil "c xiiii"? (faint) top centre; pencil "Stams, STA,
Fog. 74v" lower right margin. A green speck in the left margin beside
image-008 L11.
Features in the text: certain words are written larger with enlarged capitals
(e.g. "Si q(ui)s", "Non", "Notandu(m)", "Occasione(m)", "Nemo") at the start
of sentences; these mark new sentences within the running text. No underlining,
rubrics or interlinear glosses seen.
Tentative interpretation: continuous expository prose that alternates quoted
sentences (short direct-speech sentences introduced by an enlarged capital)
with explanation ("id est", "Sensus est", "hoc est quod dicit"). I keep it as
one stream because the hand does not separate lemma from comment by size of
script or by underlining; the enlarged capitals are the only signal.

======================================================================
SPANS SELECTED
======================================================================
All visible lines of all four column fragments. Unread: text under the patch
in image-002 (right half of L1-L4) and image-003 (L8-L12 middle/right), the
faded right half of image-002 L4-L13, and the faint top line of image-005 L14.
Column order: on each face, col. a (left) then col. b (right). The two
columns on one face do not run on directly in what I can see (col. a ends
mid-word on a folded strip and col. b starts a new thought), consistent with
lines lost at the cut edge between the bottom of one column and the top of the
next.
